title: Fourteen-minute manager primers — Ava Martinez
content:
Purpose: a compact, repeatable script for 1:1s where I need to land a micro-ask, show concrete evidence of impact, and leave the manager with a clear follow-up. Keep under 14 minutes when time is tight.

Structure (14 minutes):
  0:00–0:60s — One-sentence context + current role/commitment (anchor).
  1:00–3:00 — Top 2 wins with 1 metric each (evidence triple: metric, date, where it lives).
  3:00–6:00 — Biggest open risk or blocker (concrete example + ask).
  6:00–9:00 — Micro-ask (explicit ask + timeline + what success looks like).
  9:00–12:00 — Career signal / developmental ask (pairing, stretch project, mentorship).
  12:00–14:00 — Quick close: restate ask, confirm follow-up owner/date.

One-sentence anchor examples (pick one depending on context):
  • "I've been leading the onboarding improvements for Dedicated infra; last quarter I drove the new checklist rollout that cut onboarding time by 18%."
  • "My focus this cycle: make rollouts lower-friction for small product teams while keeping error rate <0.3%."

Top wins (pick 2) — format: headline / metric / where to find proof:
  • "Quota routing mismatch mitigation — reduced 95th p99 latency spikes for small burst jobs by ~120ms (Jan rollout). See perf dashboard: /dashboards/model-routing -> 'post-rollout' tab; JIRA PO-1267."
  • "Onboarding checklist adoption — 78% of new Dedicated customers used the checklist in first 2 weeks, average setup time down from 7.2d to 5.9d. See sheet: onboarding-adoption-2026Q1 (internal)."

Evidence quick links I will call out:
  • JIRA: PO-1283 (onboarding checklist follow-ups)
  • Confluence: Promotion Guidelines (to align talk of scope)
  • PR: people-ops-playbook/pull/47 (the checklist doc changes)

Biggest risk / example (scripted):
  • "We have a recurring gap: second-week ramp for new hires is noisy because task owners aren't assigned clearly. Example: last cohort (Feb 02) three tasks stalled for 4–5 days (tickets PO-1299, PO-1301). This delays their first independent project and stretches manager time. My suggested micro-ask: permission to run a one-off task-ownership clinic and a 1-week pilot where I pre-assign owners for cohort tasks (2–3 cohorts)."

Micro-asks (3 variations depending on risk appetite):
  • Small ask (high chance): "OK to run a single 90-minute clinic with 6 new hires and assign owners for the upcoming cohort? Will measure by 'tasks closed within week' metric and share results in 2 weeks."
  • Medium ask: "Can I run the pilot (3 cohorts) and get an extra 8 hours of product time to restructure two onboarding tasks? Outcome target: increase first-project readiness from 62% -> 78% in pilot cohorts."
  • Stretch ask (low probability): "Consider funding a short-term contractor to automate owner assignment and follow-ups for the next quarter. Budget estimate: ~$8k."

Career signal (framing / sample wording):
  • "I'm excited to grow toward a manager-of-PE/PM partnership role — specifically owning cross-functional onboarding flows and metrics. A stretch exposure I'd value: 2-week rotation with a product PM (supporting roadmap planning) or 1:1 mentoring with a senior product partner to learn prioritization tradeoffs."

Micro-asks script (explicit, short):
  • "Ask: Can I run a 1-time 90-minute task-ownership clinic next Thursday with 6 new hires?
    Timeline: run Thurs 3/11, share raw results 3/18, short follow-up in 3/25 1:1?
    Success: +20pt increase in 'tasks closed in first week' for that cohort, or at least a measurable reduction in task stall-days. If not met, I will iterate and come back with a revised plan."

Impact snapshots — quick bullets I can read aloud:
  • "Onboarding checklist adoption: cohort baseline 2025Q4 = 45% -> 78% after checklist (Feb 2026) — reference sheet.
  • 'Quota routing' mitigation: p99 latency spikes dropped 120ms for small bursts; saved ~0.7 RU/1000 requests in compute cost during peak tests (see perf dash).
  • Mentorship: ran 4 office hours for managers in Jan; 9/11 reported fewer escalations on first-week issues (survey link)."

Counter-asks / safety net to anticipate pushback:
  • If product time isn't available, propose a shorter pilot with 2 tasks only (reduce scope).
  • If manager pushes back on contractor spend, offer to run a manual 2-week process and show ROI before revisiting budget.

Calibration cues for manager (one-liners I can use if manager is short on time):
  • "I need a decision so I can start recruiting owners this week."
  • "If we can't run a pilot, I'm worried onboarding noise will slow next-quarter velocity for small teams."

Quick follow-up commitments I will make if they agree:
  1) Send calendar invite + short agenda within 24h.
  2) Share the pilot success criteria and how I'll measure within 48h.
  3) Deliver a 1–page readout 2 weeks after the pilot.

Open questions / things I still want input on:
  • Is there an existing product resource (PM/TPM) I should partner with or is this owned by people-ops?
  • How do we classify 'first-project readiness' in a way that scales across teams? (suggestion: 'can complete 1 independent story without owner unblock >80% of time')
  • Any preferred stakeholders I should cc on the pilot invite? (thinking: EM for each team, relevant PM, and on-call SRE as FYI)

Personal development tracker (what I'm working on):
  • Core skill focus this quarter: cross-team prioritization and resourcing tradeoffs.
  • Learning micro-goal: run 3 debriefs with PM partners and capture 1 decision pattern per debrief.
  • Mentor ask: monthly 1:1 with Priya to practice story-framing and negotiation.

Loose metrics I will report back in next 1:1 if pilot runs:
  • % tasks closed within 7 days (baseline 62%).
  • Mean stall-days per stalled task (target reduce by 50%).
  • Manager-reported time saved (survey)

Next steps (if manager says yes):
  1) Block 90 minutes on Thurs 3/11, invite EMs + cohort.
  2) Prepare 6–8 minute agenda + 3 templates (owner assignment, escalation path, quick checklist).
  3) Run pilot, collect metrics, short readout.

Tone reminders to self: short, confident, data-first, bias to propose a clear fallback. Avoid apologetic framing — present the pilot as a learning experiment, not as a permanent policy change.

Notes to self after practice-run with Priya (2/27):
  • Trim the intro to one line — managers tune out long context.
  • Always state the ask in one sentence before the evidence.
  • If manager is time-poor, skip the 'wins' and move straight to risk + ask + next steps.

Archive labels to add after meeting: 'pilot-approved' | 'pilot-declined' | 'needs-budget' | 'follow-up-2w'

— end —
